images.title: Three tests, cheapest first
images.alt: Flow of three validation tests run from cheapest to most expensive: find complaints, talk to five to ten people, then ask for money.
images.caption: Write down your pass line for each test before you run it.

items.label: Test 1: Find complaints
items.text: People describing the problem unprompted, in places you didn't create

items.label: Test 2: Talk to people
items.text: Five to ten people who have the problem

items.label: Test 3: Ask for money
items.text: Payment or a firm commitment before the product exists

items.label: Build the smallest version
items.text: Only what you promised, for your first buyers

images.after: Why "would you buy this?" is a bad question
images.title: Opinions vs past behaviour
images.alt: Comparison of asking whether someone would buy your idea with asking about specific things they have already done about the problem.
images.caption: Talk about the other person's life, not your idea.

columns.label: Ask about their past
points: Hard to answer with a polite lie

images.title: Keep a pre-sale fair to buyers
images.alt: Checklist for an honest pre-sale: say the product doesn't exist yet, give a realistic date, promise full refunds and keep the money aside.
images.caption: Only take money for something you will deliver or refund.

items: Say plainly that the product doesn't exist yet
Give a delivery date you have good reason to believe
Promise a full refund if you miss the date or don't build it
Pay refunds quickly, without being asked
Keep pre-sale money aside until you've delivered
Never run a fake checkout that collects card details
Read your payment processor's terms on pre-orders
